ca_methane_boulder.blurb: Methane Boulder is one large, elongated block in the Tramway part of the San Jacinto Mountains, within the zone of Shangri-La Valley called The Beach, at roughly 8,400 feet. It is a bouldering-only spot with eight problems that stretch from V1 to V9: a few at the easy end, a cluster around V4 to V6, and a pair of hard ones above V7. The south-facing side takes the sun. The block stands opposite Paul's Rock and about halfway between Blue Flame Boulder and Sharma Boulder, out on a broad, flat, open stretch of ground.

ca_mr_frosty_cave.blurb: Mr Frosty Cave is a tiny bouldering pocket in the Kindergarten Area of the Sad Boulders, near Bishop in the Eastern Sierra at about 4,000 feet. Despite the name it is an enclosed gap among the blocks rather than a true cave, with a few short problems inside and one taller problem on the entrance face. There are eight problems in all, and they skew hard: one V4, a trio at V6, then V7 and two V8s, topped by a single V12. A few yards from the parking lot, you slip through the first gap between boulders and turn right into the enclosure.

ca_headstone_base_area.blurb: Headstone Base Area is the large rocky mass that Headstone Rock sits on top of, next to Ryan Campground in Joshua Tree National Park, at about 4,330 feet. The climbing is short cracks of moderate difficulty. There are eight routes, nearly all trad: three around 5.5, four around 5.9, and one 5.11 set up as a top-rope. The lines are short, around 20 to 25 feet, so it suits quick laps and gear practice more than a long day out.

ca_hidden_slab.blurb: Hidden Slab is an 80-foot slab on the east side of the Echo Rock complex in Joshua Tree National Park, at about 4,300 feet. Eight routes cover a mix of trad, bolted and top-rope climbing, with grades from 5.7 up to 5.10. Because it faces east, it gets sun in the morning and falls into shade in the afternoon, though in late spring and early summer that shade holds off until after 3 pm. Winter sun is minimal. The base is reached with a little third-class scrambling, about 100 feet up and to the right of Bambi Meets Godzilla.

ca_peewee_rock.blurb: Peewee Rock is a low, squat formation directly opposite the Hidden Valley Campground entrance in Joshua Tree National Park, close to the much bigger Cyclops Rock, at about 4,190 feet. Most of the routes are on the right side of its north face, and a couple of boulder problems sit at the base. There are eight routes, mostly trad with two top-ropes and one bolted line, and the grades run from 5.4 through the 5.7 to 5.8 range up to several at 5.10. A short trail from the paved road leads in, and it gets few visitors despite the campground next door.

ca_lion_s_den.blurb: Lion's Den is a small crag of cracks of assorted widths plus a few faces, at about 7,700 feet in the June Lake Area of the Eastern Sierra. Climbing here is mostly trad, with two bolted routes and one top-rope, and the grades span 5.9 to 5.12: one 5.9, three at 5.10, two at 5.11 and two at 5.12. The crag faces west, so the sun reaches it in the afternoon. Its best-known crack is about 70 feet tall.

ca_king_rock.blurb: King Rock is a single large boulder in the Free Beer Area of Holcomb Valley, in the San Bernardino Mountains near Big Bear Lake, at about 7,550 feet. Its north face is smooth and coated in lichen. It has eight problems, all fairly approachable: one V0, two V1s, three V2s and a pair at V5. To find it, walk west from the smaller Beer Boulder; the whole Free Beer Area sits among trees and packs plenty of boulders into a small space.

ca_msg_boulder.blurb: MSG Boulder is a small bouldering area in Yosemite Valley, at about 3,984 feet, made up of two main boulders, one of which gives the area its name. It sits along the road leaving the Valley on the Northside Drive side, near the Wood Yard, which makes it a convenient last stop on the way out of the park. The problems range from V2 to V7, with the largest group at V4 and a couple at V6.
